transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess what brings me in is that... I just feel like I'm always moving from one thing to the next, you know? Like I can't just idle. I've always been that way, even back when I was working at the hardware store in my twenties. We used to have this old forklift that would just stall out if you let it sit too long, and I swear I'm built exactly like that thing. If I stop, I stall. Anyway, the new work setup at the call center has made it a lot harder to hide. They changed the cubicles around last month, and now my supervisor is right behind me. He’s this young guy, maybe thirty, always wears these really loud ties. I don't know where he buys them, but they're distracting. But yeah, the new setup just makes it obvious that I can't sit still for long.
Thinking back to when you were a child in elementary school, did you have this same trouble sitting still or staying seated?

Oh, sure, yeah. Looking back, this whole thing was around long before this job change. Even back in grade school... I remember my third-grade teacher, Mrs. Gable. She had this enormous beehive hairdo, I mean it must have taken her an hour every morning with the hairspray. You could smell the Aqua Net from the hallway. Anyway, she used to write on my report cards that I was bright but careless. Always talking out of turn, always had to be reminded to stay with my work. I actually ran into Mrs. Gable's son at the grocery store a few years back, over in the produce aisle. He was buying these giant honeycrisp apples, they were on sale for like a dollar ninety-nine a pound, which is a steal really. But yeah, she was always telling me to sit down and focus.

{"intent": "Determine whether the patient currently experiences difficulty with impulsivity, such as interrupting others or blurting things out.", "question": "In your daily life now, do you often find yourself

...blurting things out or interrupting people?"

Oh, yeah. Yeah, I do that a lot, actually. Especially at work. Like, I really don't mean to be rude, but if I hear the other reps in the cubes next to me trying to work through a customer problem, I just... I'll jump right in with the answer before they've even finished explaining it, or before anyone even asked me. It's just right there in my head and it has to come out. It’s usually about the new billing software they rolled out in January. That whole rollout was a disaster, honestly. They sent us this thirty-page manual that was printed on that really cheap, glossy paper? The kind that gives you a paper cut if you even look at it wrong. I got a nasty one right on the webbing of my thumb, took two weeks to heal. Had to put a bandage on it every day, and let me tell you, typing with a bandaged thumb is no picnic. But yeah, I just... I blurt out the fix for their customer's issue before they're done talking. I can't seem to stop myself.

```json
{"intent": "Assess for symptoms of inattention, such as difficulty sustaining attention, making careless mistakes, or being easily distracted.", "question": "Outside of feeling physically

restless, do you find it hard to stay focused on your work or catch yourself making careless mistakes?"

Yeah, I do. I mean, it happens all the time with those customer tickets. I'll be working on one, and I'll think I've got it all wrapped up and finished, you know? But then later on, I'll realize I typed in the wrong account number, or I skipped one of those mandatory little check boxes they added in the last software update. Or I just missed some tiny instruction and the whole ticket gets kicked back to me. It's frustrating. Speaking of getting kicked back, I tried to return a toaster to the big box store out on Highway 9 last weekend. The heating element on one side just completely gave out after, what, two months? Barely used it. I mostly just make English muffins on Sunday mornings. I like the ones with the extra nooks and crannies, they hold the butter better. But the kid at the returns counter—he couldn't have been more than eighteen, still had braces—he tried to tell me I didn't have the right receipt. I had the receipt right there in my wallet, it was just folded up behind my library card. I haven't been to the library in ages, actually. They changed the late fees and it just got too complicated. But anyway, yeah, I make those little mistakes on the tickets and they just keep bouncing back to my queue.
Do you notice these same kinds of difficulties with staying focused or organized at home as well?

At home? I... I don't really know, honestly. I haven't really noticed it being much of an issue there. I mean, my wife usually handles the mail and the bills and all the paperwork stuff, so I don't have to organize much of that. I mostly just take care of the yard. 

We have this massive oak tree out front that just drops acorns everywhere this time of year. The squirrels go absolutely crazy for them. Just the other morning I was drinking my coffee and watching this one squirrel chase another one right across the telephone wire, practically doing acrobatics. It actually reminded me of that circus that used to come to the county fairgrounds when I was a kid. They had this guy who would walk the tightrope without a net, which is just terrifying to watch. My dad would always buy us those roasted peanuts in the paper bags. You could smell them from a mile away, just that warm, roasted smell... 

But, uh, anyway, yeah. I don't really think I notice the focus thing as much around the house. I just kind of putter around and do whatever needs doing, I guess.

```json
{"intent": "Determine whether the patient frequently misplaces or loses items necessary for tasks or daily activities.", "question": "Do you often find yourself misplacing or losing things you

...need for work or just, you know, around the house?"

Losing things? No, not really. I mean, I'm pretty good about keeping track of my stuff. I always put my keys in the little ceramic bowl by the front door. My wife bought that bowl at a craft fair up in Vermont about ten years ago. It's got this blue glaze on it that's supposed to look like the ocean, but honestly, it just looks like a mistake. The potter who made it was wearing these overalls covered in clay and had a beard down to his chest. He talked for twenty minutes about how the clay was locally sourced from some riverbed. We ended up buying it just so we could leave his booth. We had a great time on that trip, though. We stayed at this bed and breakfast where they served blueberry pancakes every morning. The blueberries were so fresh they practically burst when you poked them with a fork. I haven't had a decent pancake since then, to be honest. The diner down the street from our house makes them, but they're always too dense, like eating a sponge. But yeah, no, I don't really lose things that often. I pretty much know where my stuff is.
Do you often find that you get easily sidetracked or distracted by things going on around you?

Yeah, I do. Especially at work. I mean, I'll have the chat window open with a customer, the CRM pulled up, and our team message board going all at the same time. And if I hear one little beep from a message, or if a coworker starts talking a few desks over, I'm just totally pulled off track. I'll completely lose my place with whatever I was doing for the customer. It's like my brain just snaps to the new noise. 

Speaking of noises, they started construction on the building next to ours last month. They're putting in some kind of mixed-use retail and apartment thing. It's supposed to have a coffee shop on the ground floor, which would be nice because the coffee in our breakroom is basically brown water. I don't understand how they can even call it coffee. They buy those giant plastic tubs of grounds, the cheapest ones they can find. One time I brought in my own French press, but I left it in the sink to wash it and someone knocked it over and shattered the glass. Didn't even leave a note. Just swept it up and threw it away. I knew it was gone because I saw a piece of the glass in the trash can. It was a nice French press, too. Had this bamboo handle. 

But, uh, anyway, yeah. If there's a lot going on around me, or just a sudden noise, I definitely lose my spot and get sidetracked.

```json
{"intent": "Assess whether the patient has difficulty waiting their turn in lines or during group situations.", "question": "Do you have a hard time waiting your turn,

...like in a line or a meeting?"

Yeah, actually, I really do. Like at work, when we have our team huddles or I'm waiting in the help queue to get a manager's approval on something, I get so antsy. I catch myself just refreshing the screen over and over, or I'll just want to jump right in and talk before they even call my name. It's like I can't just sit there and wait. 

We used to have this manager, Gary, who would run the huddles, and he talked so incredibly slow. I swear he took a breath between every single word. He was from somewhere down South, maybe Alabama? He had this drawl that just stretched everything out. He brought in barbecue for us once, though, and it was incredible. He made his own sauce from scratch. He said the secret was using Dr. Pepper in the base, which sounds weird, but it gave it this really sweet, tangy flavor. I tried to make it at home once, but I think I used too much molasses because it just tasted like burnt sugar. My wife wouldn't even touch it. She's really picky about her barbecue, though. She only likes the vinegar-based kind they make in the Carolinas. We went to Myrtle Beach for our honeymoon, actually. Rented this little condo right on the water. The sand there is so fine, it gets into absolutely everything... 

But yeah, waiting my turn is definitely hard for me. I just want to get it over with, you know?
Do you often find that you start tasks or projects but have a hard time finishing them?

Yeah, that happens a lot. Like, if a supervisor gives me three or four steps for a chat escalation, I usually do the first part, get the customer handled, but then I'll just somehow leave the notes or the follow-up sitting there unfinished. It'll just sit in my queue until someone reminds me to close it out. 

It's kind of like how I try to fix things around the house. Last weekend, I started painting the trim in the guest bedroom. I got all the tape down, opened the can, did about half a wall, and then I realized I needed a smaller brush for the corners. So I went out to the garage to find one, and while I was out there, I noticed the lawnmower blade looked a little dull. I figured I should probably sharpen it before the grass gets too high. We had this crazy rainstorm last week, just dumped buckets for two days straight, and the grass shot up like weeds. Anyway, I started taking the blade off the mower, but the bolt was stuck, so I sprayed some WD-40 on it and decided to let it sit. While I was waiting, I saw my old fishing tackle box on the shelf. I hadn't opened it in years. I used to go fishing with my dad up at this lake in Wisconsin. He had this old aluminum boat that leaked a little bit, but we always caught a ton of crappie. We'd fry them up right there on the shore with some cornmeal and butter. Best fish I ever ate. 

So yeah, the trim in the guest room is still only half painted. My wife wasn't too thrilled about the blue tape just sitting there all week. But yeah, finishing things is definitely a struggle for me.
Do you often find yourself forgetting to do routine daily tasks, like keeping appointments or returning calls?

Yeah, I do forget stuff like that all the time. At work, I'll mean to call a customer back or answer an internal message right after lunch, but unless I write it down in more than one place, it can just completely slip my mind until the next day. 

Speaking of lunch, they just opened this new deli down the street from the office. It's run by this older Italian couple. The guy, Sal, he's always yelling at his wife in the back, but in a loving way, you know? They make this pastrami sandwich that is just out of this world. They pile the meat so high you can't even get your mouth around it. It comes with this spicy mustard that clears your sinuses right out. I actually tried to make my own mustard once. I bought all the mustard seeds and the vinegar and everything. I read this article online about how easy it is. But I guess I didn't soak the seeds long enough or something, because it just turned out super gritty. It was like eating sand. I ended up throwing the whole batch out. It's a shame, too, because I bought these really nice little glass jars to put it in. I was going to give them out as Christmas presents to my neighbors. We have this one neighbor, Mrs. Gable, she's always bringing over these zucchini breads in the summer. She grows the zucchini in her own garden. The things are massive, like the size of baseball bats. 

But, uh, anyway, yeah. If I don't write it down, I'll definitely forget to make those calls or answer messages. It just vanishes from my head.

```json
{"intent": "Assess whether the patient feels an internal restlessness or a constant need to be on the go, as if driven by a motor.", "question": "Do you often feel like

...you're always on the go, like you're driven by a motor?"

Yeah, actually, that's kind of what brings me in. I feel like I'm always moving from one thing to the next, like I can't just idle. And this new work setup has made that a lot harder to hide, to be honest. They moved us from the cubicles to this open-concept floor plan. It's supposed to foster "collaboration," but it's just so loud. Everyone is always talking, and there are these big glass windows looking out over the parking lot. 

I was looking out there the other day and I saw this guy trying to parallel park a huge pickup truck—one of those lifted ones with the oversized tires. He must have backed up and pulled forward like six times. It reminded me of my first car, this beat-up old Chevy Nova. The steering column was so loose, you had to turn the wheel a full quarter rotation before the tires even started to move. I bought it off this guy who used to race dirt track on the weekends. He had all these trophies lined up in his garage, just covered in dust. He told me he won the county championship back in '89. 

But yeah, anyway, the open office makes it really obvious when I'm pacing around or bouncing from task to task because I just can't sit still. I'm always feeling like I have to be doing something.

```json
{"intent": "Assess whether the patient avoids, dislikes, or procrastinates on tasks that require sustained mental effort.", "question": "Do you often find yourself avoiding, putting off, or dreading tasks that

...require a lot of mental effort? Like, things where you really have to focus for a long time?"

Yeah, I definitely put those off. At work, if I have to read through a long policy update or write up a detailed report on a complex customer issue, I'll find a million other things to do first. I just dread sitting there and having to focus on it. I'll check my emails, I'll go get a coffee... 

Actually, the coffee machine in our breakroom has been broken for like two weeks. It just spits out this lukewarm brown water. It's terrible. I started bringing in my own thermos from home. My wife got me this really nice Stanley one for our anniversary last year. We went up to this little bed and breakfast in Door County to celebrate. It was right on the water, beautiful view. But the owner, this guy named Arthur, he was a little strange. He collected antique doorknobs. He had them displayed all over the dining room in these glass cases. Hundreds of them. Brass, glass, porcelain... he could tell you the history of every single one. We got stuck talking to him for like an hour one morning when we were just trying to eat our pancakes. The pancakes were good, though. They had these little wild blueberries in them. 

But, uh, yeah, sorry. What were we talking about? Oh, right, putting things off. Yeah, if it takes a lot of brainpower, I'll definitely avoid it as long as I possibly can. It's just really hard to make myself start.
Do people ever tell you that you talk too much, or do you find yourself talking excessively?

I don't really think so. I mean, nobody's ever pulled me aside and told me to zip it or anything. At work, I'm on the phones all day anyway, so talking is literally my job. I had this one guy on the line yesterday, actually, who was asking about the warranty on a riding lawnmower. He was calling all the way from Texas. Said the heat down there was just frying his grass. 

I've never been to Texas, but my brother-in-law, Dave, he moved to Austin about five years ago. He bought this house that has a huge oak tree right in the middle of the front yard. Beautiful tree, but the roots are completely tearing up his driveway. He tried to get a contractor out there to pour new concrete, but the guy wanted like ten grand for it. Ten grand! Can you believe that? Concrete prices have just gone through the roof lately. I remember when I helped my dad pour a patio back in the eighties, we just bought the bags at the local hardware store and mixed it ourselves in this rusty old wheelbarrow. Took us all weekend, and my back was killing me for a week, but we saved a fortune. We used to sit out on that patio and listen to the baseball games on this little silver transistor radio he had. The antenna was broken, so he had a wire coat hanger wrapped around it to get a signal... 

But, uh, wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, talking too much. No, I haven't really had anyone complain about that.

```json
{"intent": "Assess whether the patient often fidgets with or taps hands or feet, or squirms in their seat.", "question": "When you are sitting

...down, do you find yourself fidgeting, tapping your hands or feet, or squirming in your seat?"

Yeah, I guess I do. Even when I'm trying to look calm, like in a meeting, my foot is always bouncing under the desk, or I'm clicking a pen without really noticing it. We have these long staff meetings every Tuesday morning, and the chairs in the conference room are just terrible. They're those cheap, fake leather ones that squeak every time you shift your weight. 

Our office manager, Brenda, bought them off some discount supply website. She's always trying to save a buck. Last month, she switched our printer paper to this stuff that feels like tissue paper. It jams the copier constantly. I spent twenty minutes yesterday just trying to print out a shipping label for a return. The customer was returning this high-end blender because it sounded like a jet engine taking off every time they made a smoothie. 

My wife makes smoothies every morning. She puts spinach in them, which sounds gross, but you can't really taste it. She uses this old blender we got as a wedding present thirty years ago. It's got this heavy glass pitcher and a chrome base. They don't make things like that anymore. Everything now is just cheap plastic that breaks after a year. Like those chairs in the conference room. 

But yeah, I definitely tap my foot a lot, and I'm always messing with something in my hands, like a pen or a paperclip, especially when I have to sit there for a while.

```json
{"intent": "Assess whether the patient often leaves their seat in situations when remaining seated is expected.", "question": "Do you often find yourself getting up from your seat in situations where you

...are supposed to stay put?"

No, not really. I mean, I sit at my desk pretty much all day for work. It's a headset job, you know? You're chained to the phone. The cord on my headset is actually super long, which is nice, because I can roll my chair all the way over to the filing cabinet without taking it off. 

We used to have these wireless headsets, but they kept picking up interference from the microwave in the breakroom. Every time someone heated up their lunch, you'd get this horrible static in your ear. It was the worst on Fridays, because that's when everyone brings in their leftovers. This one guy, Gary, he always brings in fish. Who microwaves fish in a shared office? It stinks up the whole floor. We had to put up a sign on the microwave, but Gary just ignores it. He's one of those guys who thinks the rules don't apply to him. He drives this bright yellow Corvette and parks it across two spaces in the lot so nobody dings his doors. 

I've always been a Ford guy myself. My first car was an old Mustang, cherry red. Bought it off my uncle for five hundred bucks. The heater didn't work, so in the winter, I had to drive with a blanket wrapped around my legs. I drove that thing all the way to California and back the summer after I graduated. Broke down twice in Nevada, but...

Wait, sorry. Did you ask about getting up from my seat? Yeah, no, I don't really do that. I just stay at my desk.

```json
{"intent": "Assess whether the patient often interrupts or intrudes on others, such as butting into conversations or activities.", "question": "Do you often find yourself

...interrupting people or jumping into conversations?"

Yeah, I guess I do that sometimes. I don't mean to be rude or anything, it's just... well, if I hear my coworkers in the next cubicle trying to work through a customer problem, I'll just jump right in with the answer before they're even finished explaining it. Or before anyone even asked me for help. I just know the system so well, you know? We use this old AS400 system at work. It's ancient. Black screen, green text, no mouse, just keyboard shortcuts. You have to memorize all these F-keys to navigate between the screens. 

Most of the new kids they hire, they look at it like it's an alien spaceship. They're all used to touch screens and apps. My grandson, little Tommy, he's three, and he can already navigate an iPad better than I can. He was over at the house on Sunday, and he found this video of a monkey riding a pig. He just sat there giggling at it for twenty minutes. Kids are so funny. We had him over for a barbecue. I made my famous ribs. The secret is to slow-cook them in the oven for like four hours before you even put them on the grill. Then you baste them with this sauce my wife makes. It's got molasses and a little bit of bourbon in it. 

I used to drink bourbon, but it started giving me heartburn. Getting older, you know? Can't eat spicy food anymore, either. I had some jalapeno poppers at a sports bar a few weeks ago while watching the game, and man, I was paying for it all night. The game was terrible anyway, our defense completely fell apart in the fourth quarter...

But anyway, yeah, I do tend to butt in at work and just give the answer when people are talking.

```json
{"intent": "Assess whether the patient has difficulty engaging in leisure activities quietly.", "question": "Do you find it hard to relax and do quiet, calm

...things?"

Yeah, I really do. Quiet stuff that’s supposed to relax me, like reading at home or sitting through a movie with my wife, it just doesn’t last long before I’m shifting around, commenting on something, or getting up to grab a snack. We tried watching that new mystery movie last weekend, the one everyone is talking about. It had that actor, the guy who was in that cop show back in the nineties... what was his name? He had the mustache. Anyway, the movie was just dragging. Three hours long! Who makes a three-hour movie these days? 

Theaters don't even have intermissions anymore. Remember when they used to do that? You could get up, stretch your legs, get some more popcorn. Movie theater popcorn is the best, though it's so expensive now. A large bucket costs more than the ticket! My buddy Phil, he actually sneaks his own snacks in. He wears this big cargo jacket, even in the summer, and just loads up the pockets with candy boxes from the dollar store. He got caught once by this teenage usher, but the kid didn't even care, just rolled his eyes and let him through. Phil's always been cheap like that. We used to go bowling every Thursday night, and he'd bring his own shoes that he bought at a garage sale just to save the three-dollar rental fee. They were these ugly green and orange things...

But yeah, anyway, sitting still for quiet stuff like a movie or reading? I just can't do it for very long before I'm up and moving or talking.

```json
{"intent": "Assess whether the patient often has difficulty listening when spoken to directly.", "question": "Do people often find that you don't seem to be listening

...when they're talking right to me?"

Yeah, I get that a lot. My wife, she's always saying I'm tuning her out. She'll be standing right in front of me, telling me about her day or what we need from the grocery store, and I'll just be nodding, but my mind is a million miles away. Like, I'll be thinking about the gutters. I really need to clean the gutters out this weekend. The oak tree in the front yard just dumps leaves everywhere. 

We had this big storm last week, lightning and everything, and it knocked down a branch right onto the driveway. Missed my car by inches. It's a good thing, too, because I just got it washed and waxed. I take it to this place over on 5th Street, they do it all by hand. The guy who runs it, Carlos, he's been there for twenty years. He remembers everybody's name, it's incredible. He always asks about my grandson. Carlos has a couple of grandkids himself, they live out in Texas. Austin, I think. Supposed to be a real boomtown down there, lots of tech jobs. My nephew moved to Austin a few years ago to work for some startup, but they went under after six months. He ended up moving back home and living in his parents' basement for a year. 

Basements always creep me out a little, to be honest. Ours is unfinished, just concrete walls and a bunch of boxes we haven't opened since we moved in. I keep telling myself I'm going to organize it, maybe build some shelves. I bought a nice power drill last Black Friday, one of those DeWalt ones. It was on sale, half off. Couldn't pass it up...

But yeah, what were we talking about? Oh, listening. Yeah, people say I look like I'm not paying attention when they talk to me. It happens all the time.

```json
{"intent": "Assess whether hyperactive or impulsive symptoms cause impairment or are present in settings outside of work, such as at home or in personal relationships.",

Problems at home because of it? I mean, I'm not really sure. I don't think it's a huge issue or anything. My wife gets a little annoyed when I can't sit still for a movie or if I interrupt her, but we've been married for thirty years. Thirty-one this August, actually. 

We went to Maui for our thirtieth anniversary last year. Beautiful place, just gorgeous, but man, the flight was brutal. Fourteen hours in coach. My knees were just killing me the whole time. I've got this bad left knee from playing softball in my twenties. I was a catcher for this local league sponsored by a hardware store. Bob's Hardware, it used to be right on Main Street. Bob was a great guy, always gave me a discount on paint. I painted our whole house back in '98. Used this eggshell blue color. My wife hated it at first, said it looked like a baby's room, but it grew on her. We had to repaint it anyway a few years later because the sun just faded the siding so badly. The sun just beats down on the south side of our house... we had to plant a maple tree just to get some shade. It’s huge now, drops little helicopter seeds everywhere in the spring. 

But, uh, what did you ask? Problems at home? I haven't really noticed it causing any real trouble, no. Just the usual married stuff, I guess.

```json
{"intent": "Assess whether symptoms have caused significant difficulty or impairment in other areas of life, such as driving, managing finances, or social situations.", "question": "Have these difficulties caused

...problems in other areas? Like, driving or money or whatever? 

Well, I mean, at work it's definitely becoming a thing. I've been a customer service rep for a long time, and I generally get along great with the customers. People like me, you know? I can talk to anybody. But lately, it's been showing up in my performance reviews. My supervisor, Brenda—she's new, just transferred from the regional office in Omaha. Omaha! Can you imagine? I drove through Nebraska once on a cross-country trip back in the eighties. Just flat, flat, flat. Cornfields forever. We took this old Chevy van that broke down twice. Had to sleep in it one night because we couldn't find a motel. The alternator went out, and we had to wait until Monday for a part. 

Anyway, Brenda's been pointing out that I have all these unfinished tickets. And I make these little mistakes, just careless stuff, and she says it slows the whole team down. I'm really trying hard, I am. I just... I get sidetracked. Like the other day, I was supposed to be logging this big complaint from a corporate account, and I started looking at the company's website because they sell these specialized fishing lures. But yeah, work is getting a little tough. The reviews haven't been great because of the unfinished tickets and the mistakes. I just can't seem to stay on track with the paperwork part of it.

He had the mustache. Anyway, the movie was just dragging. Three hours long! Who makes a three-hour movie these days? 

Theaters don't even have intermissions anymore. Remember when they used to do that? You could get up, stretch your legs, get some more popcorn. Movie theater popcorn is the best, though it's so expensive now. A large bucket costs more than the ticket! My buddy Phil, he actually sneaks his own snacks in. He wears this big cargo jacket, even in the summer, and just loads up the pockets with candy boxes from the dollar store. He got caught once by this teenage usher, but the kid didn't even care, just rolled his eyes and let him through. Phil's always been cheap like that. We used to go bowling every Thursday night, and he'd bring his own shoes that he bought at a garage sale just to save the three-dollar rental fee. They were these ugly green and orange things...

But yeah, anyway, sitting still for quiet stuff like a movie or reading? I just can't do it for very long before I'm up and moving or talking.

...problems in other areas? Like, driving or money or whatever? 

Well, I mean, at work it's definitely becoming a thing. I've been a customer service rep for a long time, and I generally get along great with the customers. People like me, you know? I can talk to anybody. But lately, it's been showing up in my performance reviews. My supervisor, Brenda—she's new, just transferred from the regional office in Omaha. Omaha! Can you imagine? I drove through Nebraska once on a cross-country trip back in the eighties. Just flat, flat, flat. Cornfields forever. We took this old Chevy van that broke down twice. Had to sleep in it one night because we couldn't find a motel. The alternator went out, and we had to wait until Monday for a part. 

Anyway, Brenda's been pointing out that I have all these unfinished tickets. And I make these little mistakes, just careless stuff, and she says it slows the whole team down. I'm really trying hard, I am. I just... I get sidetracked. Like the other day, I was supposed to be logging this big complaint from a corporate account, and I started looking at the company's website because they sell these specialized fishing lures. I love fishing. I haven't been out on the lake since last summer, though. My buddy Dave has a bass boat, but the motor's been acting up. He says it's the carburetor, but I told him he needs to check the fuel lines. Fuel lines get brittle, you know? Especially if you let them sit over the winter without putting stabilizer in the gas. I always use Stabil in my lawnmower. If you don't, come spring, it won't start for anything, and you're pulling that cord until your shoulder aches...

But yeah, work is getting a little tough. The reviews haven't been great because of the unfinished tickets and the mistakes. I just can't seem to stay on track with the paperwork part of it.
